attempts.summary: Configured port mirroring so node3 receives a copy of all traffic exchanged between node1 and node2 on their shared segment (eth1, 192.168.50.0/24), while the original node1<->node2 traffic continues unaffected. Implementation: node1 (the SONiC device, one of the two conversant hosts) runs a Linux tc clsact classifier on eth1 with two flower filters (matching frames to/from node2's MAC) that use a mirred "mirror" action (non-disruptive copy) to duplicate matching L2 frames into a GRE-tap (gretap) tunnel device 'mirror0'. That tunnel carries the mirrored copies over the separate management network (eth0, 10.100.40.0/24) to a matching gretap device on node3, where a capture on 'mirror0' shows the mirrored node1<->node2 packets even though node3 is not one of the two endpoints and its direct eth1 capture stays empty (confirming the segment is a real switched domain, not a hub, and that mirroring - not flooding - is responsible). Baseline testing (before mirroring) confirmed node3 saw zero node1<->node2 packets on eth1 directly; after mirroring was enabled, node3's mirror0 interface captured all ICMP request/reply pairs, and concurrent pings showed 0% packet loss, proving the original path was undisturbed. Required a fix for RHEL7's default firewalld/conntrack behavior: GRE (protocol 47) was being dropped as ctstate INVALID because nf_conntrack_proto_gre wasn't loaded; loading it (persisted via /etc/modules-load.d) plus a permanent firewalld protocol=gre allow resolved delivery to node3. All configuration (eth1 addressing, gretap devices, tc filters) was persisted via systemd oneshot services (node1: mirror-setup.service; node3: mirror-recv.service) and NetworkManager ifcfg files (node2, node3) so it survives reboot. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id + working mirror/traffic) on all three nodes, restarted node1, then node2, then node3 one at a time (native `reboot`, non-blocking ack), polled each until reachable again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and re-verified full mirroring/traffic health after each individual restart and once more after all three had cycled.
